hypothesis: Add one task-agnostic capped inverse-frequency token calibration pass after the Parent's unchanged five corpus-pretraining epochs, so infrequent lexical SMILES targets exert more teacher-forcing pressure while the frequency-normalized objective keeps overall gradient scale bounded and leaves the vocabulary and downstream policy interface unchanged.
method_thesis: Train a task-agnostic autoregressive SMILES model only on the allowed unlabeled corpus, freeze a copy as the prior, and restart a trainable agent for each independent objective session. Generate the first proposals ancestrally, then use returned oracle scores to apply top-fraction prior-regularized likelihood updates to the agent. Whenever the recent reward trajectory shows sustained improvement, run Beam Enumeration on the current agent without calling the oracle: expand its most probable partial token trajectories, convert chemically interpretable partial strings into connected molecular substructures, and retain a small task-local pool of recurrent motifs. Fill subsequent evaluator-announced batches by sampling complete SMILES de novo from the agent and locally rejecting any valid novel sample that lacks every pooled motif; canonicalize and remove already evaluated or within-batch duplicates before submission. The enumerated objects are transient partial token trajectories, not whole candidate molecules, and neither they nor any corpus molecule are scored, ranked, retrieved, or submitted as a finite library. Thus oracle feedback changes both the policy and a dynamic structural gate on fresh generation, concentrating the 290 adaptive calls on chemistry expressed by successful policy updates while the only success criterion remains the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores.

method_tags.proposal_mechanism: dynamic top-probability beam expansion for motif extraction followed by motif-gated rejection sampling of complete de novo SMILES
method_tags.representation: tokenized SMILES plus RDKit-extracted connected substructures from partial token trajectories

activation_observables.measurement: After the unchanged fifth Parent epoch and before calibration, retain an exact state digest. Define the lexical-tail audit set solely from training-split target counts as the bottom quartile of training-supported non-special vocabulary types, ordered by count and token index. On every occurrence of those same types in the fixed held-out split, record target count, mean correct-target probability, mean NLL, and top-5 inclusion under both the exact pre-calibration snapshot and the published post-calibration state. For each state compute the macro average of per-type NLL over tail types observed in heldout data and report its exponential, the tail-type geometric-mean correct-target probability, together with the paired change, every derived class weight, weighted calibration exposure, and pre/post ordinary ancestral completion, valid-canonical, and unique-valid rates from the same preparation-seeded sampling stream. Activation requires nonzero held-out tail exposure, a nonconstant realized class-weight profile, and an aggregate increase in tail-type geometric-mean correct-target probability; overall held-out NLL and ancestral support are safety diagnostics rather than substitutes for the registered tail movement.

applicability_conditions: The corpus-derived vocabulary must contain a nontrivial lexical frequency tail, and at least some of its bottom-quartile token types must occur in the fixed held-out split; absent held-out tail occurrences make the registered support mediator unmeasurable.

Infrequent corpus tokens must represent reusable SMILES syntax or chemistry rather than corrupt or idiosyncratic strings. Upweighting noisy rare targets can broaden the wrong support and reduce canonical validity.

A single capped calibration pass must be enough to move rare-token conditional support without erasing the common-token grammar learned during the unchanged five Parent epochs; the frequency-weighted mean normalization and maximum weight of 2.0 bound that tradeoff.

The training-split token counts must reasonably represent the lexical tail encountered by downstream ancestral generation and graph-equivalent replay. This mechanism does not create tokens absent from the serialized vocabulary or molecular graphs absent from corpus support.

Preparation remains strictly task agnostic: token counts, weights, calibration examples, held-out audits, and sampling diagnostics use only the allowed unlabeled corpus, its fixed split, the preparation seed, and the assigned device, with no task identity, oracle score, or online memory.

Downstream benefit is most plausible when sparse but valid lexical events are a bottleneck for reward-reachable trajectories. It may not help objectives limited instead by stale graph memory, absent molecular support, beam-motif quality, or acquisition selectivity.

The unchanged two-file artifact, vocabulary order, BOS/EOS/padding semantics, model dimensions, and maximum length must continue to instantiate identical frozen-prior and task-local agent copies in every downstream session.

This mechanism is distinct from refuted checkpoint selection in n-1e6816bbc389 and from graph-equivalent traversal calibration in n-c96561799890: it changes the training influence of corpus token types, not which existing epoch is published or which serialization of a graph is shown. No Knowledge-only or refuted cluster in the supplied Curate history contains this frequency-weighted causal claim.
research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism did not produce its claimed intermediate behavior if the realized class weights are constant, if no bottom-quartile lexical target receives nonzero calibration or held-out exposure, if the published state does not differ from the exact post-epoch-five Parent snapshot, or if the pooled tail-type geometric-mean correct-target probability on the identical held-out contexts fails to increase after calibration. A verified tail-support increase with preserved execution but a benchmark gain below the registered threshold would instead mean the mechanism activated without useful downstream transfer.

research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Parent n-a1feb7fbd3ae learns its task-agnostic prior with an unweighted token-level cross-entropy objective, so each lexical type influences preparation only in direct proportion to how often it occurs. Across its three preparation seeds the resulting policy completes all 768 registered ancestral draws but produces only 656 valid unique canonical molecules, leaving 112 complete draws unusable, while its weakest task means remain median_2 at 0.21139955631803173 and sitagliptin_mpo at 0.2611605684579006. Node n-1e6816bbc389 shows that selecting among the same unweighted trajectory does not address the limitation: the terminal Parent checkpoint has the best measured unique-valid support on all three seeds and is selected every time. Node n-c96561799890 further shows that broad graph-traversal calibration moves a different mediator but raises pooled ordinary held-out NLL by 0.012454269993737 and leaves post-calibration unique-valid rates between 0.59375 and 0.671875. The behavior targeted here is therefore count-proportional undertraining of the lexical tail inside the otherwise productive Parent prior, not checkpoint choice, graph serialization, or any online mechanism.

applicability_conditions: The intended all-supported-token claim is not applicable to these three fixed splits as registered: their true bottom quartiles have no held-out occurrences, so no conditional-support direction can be estimated without changing the audit population or data split.

The only reproducible positive claim applies to the implementation's separate count-at-least-512 proxy: 30 eligible lexical types, an eight-type audit set, one 485-step continued-optimizer pass, and 293-317 held-out proxy occurrences per seed. It does not transfer evidentially to vocabulary types with fewer than 512 training targets.

The proxy result is task agnostic in the observed execution. Counts, weights, preparation updates, held-out audits, state digests, and ancestral samples use only the allowed corpus, preparation seed, and device, and all receipts report zero calibration or audit oracle submissions.

The two-file artifact schema, vocabulary serialization, model dimensions, and online source interface remain intact, but operational compatibility is only partial: all three artifacts load and twelve objective sessions finish, while three sessions cannot fill a later novel batch.

A future test of the registered mechanism requires a corpus/split with at least one true bottom-quartile held-out occurrence and an implementation that constructs and weights the quartile from all count-positive non-special types. The present evidence supports neither beneficial nor adverse movement of that true-tail geometric-mean probability.

Even for the proxy mechanism, preservation of ordinary grammar and downstream proposal support is not established. Applicability is weaker when an additional pass reduces completion or valid novelty, or when beam-motif gating and replay already concentrate the proposal distribution.

possible_failure_causes: The registered support mediator has no opportunity on these fixed splits. The actual bottom-quartile types occur only 1-6 times in training and zero times in heldout data on every seed, directly violating the activation requirement for nonzero held-out tail exposure and making their paired support statistics undefined.

The hard-coded minimum training count of 512 changes both the intervention and the audit population. It excludes every registered-tail type, gives those types the same raw weight 1.0 and a normalized weight slightly below 1.0, then labels eight much more frequent tokens as the tail. The proxy's positive movement therefore cannot rescue the intended mechanism.

Even within the eight-token proxy, improvement is aggregate rather than uniform. For example, seed 0 decreases [S+] mean probability and worsens token 7 mean NLL, seed 1 worsens Br mean NLL and lowers its top-5 inclusion, and seed 2 lowers [n+] mean probability and worsens [S+] mean NLL. Shared-parameter redistribution can oppose individual token outcomes despite the proxy geometric mean increasing.

The extra continued-optimizer pass weakens general support on one preparation. Seed 1 loses 20/256 completions and 34/256 unique valid molecules, and across seeds the ordinary held-out NLL rises by 0.001115349518260357 while unique-valid support falls from 656/768 to 631/768. Upweighting the proxy classes may trade against common grammar or act as an uncontrolled sixth epoch.

Three of fifteen formal task sessions exhaust the unchanged ancestral novelty/gating path before their oracle budgets are complete. Because the online suffix is byte-identical to the Parent, the changed published prior is a plausible contributor, but the artifacts do not isolate whether failure arises from reduced prior support, interaction with the motif gate, replay-driven concentration, or their combination.

applicability_conditions: The intended all-supported-token claim is not applicable to these three fixed splits as registered: their true bottom quartiles have no held-out occurrences, so no conditional-support direction can be estimated without changing the audit population or data split.

The only reproducible positive claim applies to the implementation's separate count-at-least-512 proxy: 30 eligible lexical types, an eight-type audit set, one 485-step continued-optimizer pass, and 293-317 held-out proxy occurrences per seed. It does not transfer evidentially to vocabulary types with fewer than 512 training targets.

The proxy result is task agnostic in the observed execution. Counts, weights, preparation updates, held-out audits, state digests, and ancestral samples use only the allowed corpus, preparation seed, and device, and all receipts report zero calibration or audit oracle submissions.

The two-file artifact schema, vocabulary serialization, model dimensions, and online source interface remain intact, but operational compatibility is only partial: all three artifacts load and twelve objective sessions finish, while three sessions cannot fill a later novel batch.

A future test of the registered mechanism requires a corpus/split with at least one true bottom-quartile held-out occurrence and an implementation that constructs and weights the quartile from all count-positive non-special types. The present evidence supports neither beneficial nor adverse movement of that true-tail geometric-mean probability.

Even for the proxy mechanism, preservation of ordinary grammar and downstream proposal support is not established. Applicability is weaker when an additional pass reduces completion or valid novelty, or when beam-motif gating and replay already concentrate the proposal distribution.

applicability_conditions: The corpus-derived vocabulary must contain a nontrivial lexical frequency tail, and at least some of its bottom-quartile token types must occur in the fixed held-out split; absent held-out tail occurrences make the registered support mediator unmeasurable.

Infrequent corpus tokens must represent reusable SMILES syntax or chemistry rather than corrupt or idiosyncratic strings. Upweighting noisy rare targets can broaden the wrong support and reduce canonical validity.

A single capped calibration pass must be enough to move rare-token conditional support without erasing the common-token grammar learned during the unchanged five Parent epochs; the frequency-weighted mean normalization and maximum weight of 2.0 bound that tradeoff.

The training-split token counts must reasonably represent the lexical tail encountered by downstream ancestral generation and graph-equivalent replay. This mechanism does not create tokens absent from the serialized vocabulary or molecular graphs absent from corpus support.

Preparation remains strictly task agnostic: token counts, weights, calibration examples, held-out audits, and sampling diagnostics use only the allowed unlabeled corpus, its fixed split, the preparation seed, and the assigned device, with no task identity, oracle score, or online memory.

Downstream benefit is most plausible when sparse but valid lexical events are a bottleneck for reward-reachable trajectories. It may not help objectives limited instead by stale graph memory, absent molecular support, beam-motif quality, or acquisition selectivity.

The unchanged two-file artifact, vocabulary order, BOS/EOS/padding semantics, model dimensions, and maximum length must continue to instantiate identical frozen-prior and task-local agent copies in every downstream session.

This mechanism is distinct from refuted checkpoint selection in n-1e6816bbc389 and from graph-equivalent traversal calibration in n-c96561799890: it changes the training influence of corpus token types, not which existing epoch is published or which serialization of a graph is shown. No Knowledge-only or refuted cluster in the supplied Curate history contains this frequency-weighted causal claim.
research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism did not produce its claimed intermediate behavior if the realized class weights are constant, if no bottom-quartile lexical target receives nonzero calibration or held-out exposure, if the published state does not differ from the exact post-epoch-five Parent snapshot, or if the pooled tail-type geometric-mean correct-target probability on the identical held-out contexts fails to increase after calibration. A verified tail-support increase with preserved execution but a benchmark gain below the registered threshold would instead mean the mechanism activated without useful downstream transfer.
research_intent.implementation_change: Preserve the Parent's corpus reservoir, fixed split, vocabulary construction and order, GRU architecture, optimizer, learning rate, dropout, deterministic batch order, five ordinary token-level training epochs, artifact filenames and schema contract, and every online generation, feedback, graph-memory, randomized-replay, beam, motif, acquisition, canonicalization, duplicate-rejection, and oracle path. Immediately after epoch five, digest the exact Parent-equivalent state and count predicted target tokens in the training split. For each non-special lexical token with count c, derive raw weight min(2.0, max(1.0, sqrt(median_lexical_count / c))); give ordinary special targets raw weight 1.0 and PAD zero, then divide non-PAD weights by their training-target-frequency-weighted mean. Run exactly one additional preparation-seeded pass over the same stored corpus paths with the continuing optimizer, replacing only the per-token reduction by the resulting normalized weighted mean. Publish that calibrated state through the unchanged smiles_prior.pt plus smiles_policy.json interface and add complete count, weight, exposure, exact-state-digest, paired held-out tail-support, ordinary held-out NLL, ancestral-support, and zero-oracle diagnostics.
research_intent.mechanism: Add one task-agnostic capped inverse-frequency token calibration pass after the Parent's unchanged five corpus-pretraining epochs, so infrequent lexical SMILES targets exert more teacher-forcing pressure while the frequency-normalized objective keeps overall gradient scale bounded and leaves the vocabulary and downstream policy interface unchanged.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Parent n-a1feb7fbd3ae learns its task-agnostic prior with an unweighted token-level cross-entropy objective, so each lexical type influences preparation only in direct proportion to how often it occurs. Across its three preparation seeds the resulting policy completes all 768 registered ancestral draws but produces only 656 valid unique canonical molecules, leaving 112 complete draws unusable, while its weakest task means remain median_2 at 0.21139955631803173 and sitagliptin_mpo at 0.2611605684579006. Node n-1e6816bbc389 shows that selecting among the same unweighted trajectory does not address the limitation: the terminal Parent checkpoint has the best measured unique-valid support on all three seeds and is selected every time. Node n-c96561799890 further shows that broad graph-traversal calibration moves a different mediator but raises pooled ordinary held-out NLL by 0.012454269993737 and leaves post-calibration unique-valid rates between 0.59375 and 0.671875. The behavior targeted here is therefore count-proportional undertraining of the lexical tail inside the otherwise productive Parent prior, not checkpoint choice, graph serialization, or any online mechanism.
